second_order: explaining r/place as this year’s button
theme_note: Participants orient one another to the live canvas; the practice varies from introducing tile placement to asking and answering through the familiar button comparison.

second_order: teaming up with hockey fans on what to put up
theme_note: Participants recruit this room and other hockey fan communities into a shared canvas effort; proposals vary between a Preds mark, rival-directed slogans, and reluctant cooperation with rivals.
This single code preserves the distinct practice of requesting a drawable pixel-style team design.

second_order: turning logo pictures and grids into a shared target
theme_note: Participants make the desired mark usable by offering a colour-correct picture, choosing a common grid, and redesigning the incomplete space.

second_order: keeping updates, choices, and duplicate efforts together
theme_note: Participants centralize a scattered project in one update comment, demand a clear goal, poll a choice, and redirect a duplicate thread; what varies is whether coordination is informational, decisional, or spatial.

second_order: learning, placing, and correcting pixels together
theme_note: Participants teach placement mechanics, report and deconflict their dots, correct mistakes, and persuade inaccurate placers to move; the practice ranges from basic instruction to local repair.

second_order: moving the logo when other work takes the spot
theme_note: Participants repeatedly relocate, shrink, or reconsider the logo as the Void and neighbouring work occupy space; later accounts vary between blaming the move and recounting others taking the vacated spot.

second_order: sharing scripts, then turning them off
theme_note: Participants use an automated placement script to compensate for limited hands, distribute revisions, warn that old copies interfere, and finally stop automation for manual choices.

second_order: making peace and drawing boundaries with neighbours
theme_note: Participants avoid invasion, seek truces, compare deals with raids, negotiate exact borders, and reject a proposed takedown in favour of keeping their own mark; positions vary from anticipating turf war to celebrating agreement.

second_order: trading help after setting rivalries aside
theme_note: Visitors and Preds participants offer, accept, and promise reciprocal help across community lines; the exchanges vary among hockey rivals, neighbours helping a move, and requests to return assistance elsewhere.

second_order: mourning the finish and saying they Perded it up
theme_note: Participants evaluate the incomplete mark, mourn the cutoff, remember the shared attempt as fun, blame low numbers or greed, joke that they Perded it up, and explain afterward why further work is pointless.

second_order: showing the logo and saying we did it
theme_note: After placement closes, participants present image posts and call the first position complete; the claims range from an ambiguous “We did it” to an explicitly named Preds logo.

second_order: turning neighbouring logos into a possible playoff matchup
theme_note: This single code preserves a distinct joke that reads nearby canvas marks through the community’s hockey season.

second_order: looking for the logo in saved frames and albums
theme_note: Participants seek the logo in saved canvas frames, ask where it ended up, and pass along an album; what varies is whether the artifact is located, requested, or merely linked.

second_order: wanting their spot even though it is not real
theme_note: Two near-duplicate posts preserve an imagined version of the community’s spot after the live canvas has ended; one names Place explicitly and one remains more ambiguous.

second_order: weighing attacks against keeping their own logo
theme_note: Participants entertain strikes or opportunistic takeover but also defer them and warn that rivals could destroy their own work; the practice varies from a shouted opening to attack to explicit risk restraint.
